literal.prompt: С каким чувством прежде всего связан язык?

sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.individualGround: 14.1L64 explicitly associates tongue with gustation(taste),uniquely slot3. Balance encoded by inner earL135;hearing uses ear/cochlear neural pathwayL101–107;vision photoreceptorsL43,59. “Прежде всего” is sensory association,not claim tongue has no touch/temperature or other functions;23.3L46 confirms those additional roles. Four recognized senses form comparable alternatives,not body-function or grammar mismatch.

sourcesLocators.claimGround: Gustation is special sense associated with tongue; papillae contain taste buds with specialized gustatory receptor cells. Does not claim all papilla types have taste buds.
Inner-ear hair cells encode head position/movement; utricle/saccule and semicircular canals contribute balance, neural signals pass to brainstem/cerebellum.
Outer ear directs sound, middle ossicles transmit it, cochlea transduces to neural signals relayed to brain; hearing includes all these structures and neural pathways.
Retinal light-sensitive cells are photoreceptors; vision involves their activation and sensory-to-neural processing. “Begins” means receptor transduction,not denial of prior light refraction.

Tongue facilitates taste, chewing, swallowing and vocalization; muscles position food for chewing/bolus/swallowing,flexibility supports speech. Taste-bearing papillae distinguished from filiform touch papillae atL51–52.

sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.individualGround: Both stated sentences are factually supported:14.1L64–67 taste buds contain receptor cells;23.3L46–50 and163–168 give speech,chewing,swallowing. Two sentences and withinwordlimit. However Explanation never directly states the correct sense (“вкус”/“со вкусом”). Its first sentence names taste buds and receptor cells, and second lists speech,chewing,swallowing; association of tongue with the sense of taste is only inferred from the adjective “вкусовые”. The contract requires explanation to directly name the correct answer,not only related anatomical structures.
